Mock exam day: what you get.

Adaptive, like the real exam: 85 to 150 questions, ending when your result is clear or at 150, with no going back. About 2.5 hours, a 5-hour limit, and optional breaks at 2 and 3.5 hours with the clock running. Then a readiness report for each area, and your plan rebalances around it.

How do you feel about a full-length mock: A) ready or B) nervous? Reply A or B. Save this for exam prep.

Mocks are built into every plan. See plans: https://www.nclexready.com.au/pricing?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=mock-day

#NCLEXRN #NCLEX #NCLEXPrep #AHPRA #OBA #IQN #NurseLife

A near miss. No one was hurt. Do you report it?

Report it. Near misses are reported precisely because no one was hurt this time. The review looks for system causes, not blame. If harm happens, explain honestly, apologise and say what will change. An apology is generally not an admission of liability.

Have you seen a near miss go unreported? A) yes B) no. Reply A or B.
